correctness.rationale: With p=p₁,q=p₂,r=p₃, the projector I−aaᵀ yields the stated quadratic form M in x=d₁−d₃,y=d₂−d₃; its off-diagonal entry is pq−r and (1−p)(1−q)=pq+r, giving det M=4pqr. The cube fibers in d₃ have length (1−w)₊, w=max(|x|,|y|,|x−y|)=(|x|+|y|+|x−y|)/2. The ellipse stays in w≤1 through exactly t₀, since its maxima of those three linear absolute values are t(1−q), t(1−p), t(1−r), each divided by 2√(pqr). Beyond t₀, the integrals of (1−w)₊ and 1−w differ strictly on a positive-area open set. The disk change of variables has Jacobian t²/(2√(pqr)); integrating absolute linear forms with disk first absolute moment 4/3 gives the stated cubic. At one zero coordinate the gap is |d₁−Z| with Z the independent weighted sum of the other uniforms; subtracting the two end losses against the triangular endpoint densities gives 2t−t³/(3uv). At two zeros the uniform difference gives 2t−t². Layer cake gives the claimed thresholds, with logarithmic divergence at the critical exponents. For positive η the Schur complement at λ uses a positive denominator ≥1−η. At λ=0 the complement is PSD, and at λ=η its eigenvalues are ≤η before subtracting λI; each ordered eigenvalue minus λ decreases strictly. The two roots, counted with multiplicity, are the two small full-matrix eigenvalues by inertia. Weyl on the 2×2 complement bounds each error as claimed, and hence the normalized gap error is uniform. No fixed-positive-η polynomial is inferred.
residual_risks: The moment claim concerns the compression, not finite-η inverse moments; the limit is first η→0, then t→0. No expert attestation or Lean certificate is inferred.

value.rationale: The exact small-gap exponent changes at coordinate-aligned orientations in the smallest nontrivial model of a randomly split null space. That change determines precisely which inverse moments are finite. The coefficients and sharp CDF interval quantify what a general gap bound misses and provide a direct benchmark when near-degenerate orientations matter.
